threatModel.summary: Jubarte is an in-process Rust DOCX comparison, editing, inspection, conversion and revision-processing engine. Rust byte APIs are exposed through a native CLI, PyO3 Python bindings and Python CLI, wasm-bindgen browser/Node bindings and a Node CLI. An optional Python MCP server exposes document tools over stdio with a directory capability. Inputs flow through package admission into OPC/XML processing, comparison/editing/layout, then returned bytes or caller-selected filesystem outputs. Rendering additionally reads installed fonts and maintains a host font index; these operations have authority separate from document publication. Explicit native self-update retrieves GitHub release assets and replaces the executable. Tag-driven GitHub Actions builds and publishes releases. Evidence: src/lib.rs:7-30; jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/__main__.py:5-27; jubarte-wasm/src/lib.rs:7-28; jubarte-wasm/cli/bin/jubarte-redlines.mjs:16-21; jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:67-108,373-381; src/convert/font.rs:3090-3107; src/update.rs:186-257; .github/workflows/release.yml:15-21,230-245,356-369.
assets: Confidential document contents, media, revision histories, author/comment metadata and rendered text. Read/inspection tools intentionally disclose these to their caller; edit/render workflows write derived DOCX, PDFs, PNGs and reports. Evidence: src/lib.rs:17-28; jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:131-150,185-218,229-255.

Integrity of source-bound edits and explicitly selected output files. Legacy EditPlan source_sha256 is optional and checked when present; CLI additionally provides source-recheck machinery. Evidence: src/edit.rs:5-13,2081-2089; src/bin/jubarte.rs:1642-1655.

Host memory and CPU consumed by untrusted ZIP/XML, images, fonts, legacy DOC and document layout/comparison. Admission bounds input structures but is not a whole-process resource sandbox. Evidence: SECURITY.md:39-77; src/admission.rs:63-99,439-553.

MCP root contents and output integrity; host-installed font files and font-index metadata; updater executable integrity; release signing and GitHub publication authority. Evidence: src/publication.rs:146-205; src/convert/font.rs:2633-2652,3098-3107,3155-3168,3213-3229; src/update.rs:198-207; .github/workflows/release.yml:234-235,261-307,356-369.
trustBoundaries: Untrusted document producer to engine: complete package bytes enter admission before representative comparison/rendering paths. Default limits are 64 MiB compressed, 10,000 entries, 64 MiB per part, 256 MiB total inflated and XML depth 256; comparison limits are 512 MiB compressed/per part and 2 GiB total, with the same entry/depth caps. Python/WASM comparison options apply explicit overrides to the comparison settings. Admission checks ZIP defects, canonical part identity, encryption/compression, declared and actual inflation and XML policy. Evidence: src/admission.rs:63-99,137-153,439-553; src/document_comparer.rs:4903-4918,6530-6559; src/convert/mod.rs:769-778; jubarte-python/src/lib.rs:65-79; jubarte-wasm/src/lib.rs:63-74.

Raw XML caller to DOM: checked parsing applies XML policy, while public infallible parse_xdocument is a lower-level permissive interface whose caller must gate untrusted XML. The tag defaults are 1,024 attributes, 1,024-byte attribute names, 64 MiB raw/decoded values and 128 MiB complete start tags. Evidence: src/xmllinq/parse.rs:44-57,91-98,111-134.

Agent/client to edit engine: plans select exact anchors against the untouched source; optional legacy source hash rejects stale bytes. This establishes document consistency, not authentication or approval of the requested change. Evidence: src/edit.rs:5-24,2073-2094.

Native CLI/operator to local filesystem: explicitly selected paths use ambient authority. The Rust publisher holds destination-parent handles, stages and verifies complete bytes, and commits each file separately; failures report already committed files. Existing destinations require overwrite authorization. This is not the MCP directory confinement boundary. Evidence: src/publication.rs:83-130,168-205,211-225,421-480.

MCP client to document filesystem: --root defaults to process cwd and is expanded/resolved once; build_server opens a native OutputRoot capability. All document loads and outputs route through that held directory. Python resolve/is_relative_to checks provide early diagnostics; actual I/O is capability relative. Outputs reject unsafe relative names, escaping resolution and output symlinks, with overwrite false by default. All connected stdio clients share this root and the registered read/write tools; ToolAnnotations are hints, not per-client authorization. Evidence: jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:54-55,67-108,152-160,373-381; jubarte-python/src/lib.rs:1244-1278; src/publication.rs:146-199,228-245,431-463.

Markdown author to CLI image loader: document image names are percent decoded, URL schemes are refused and resolved targets must remain inside --resource-path or the Markdown file's parent, falling back to cwd. A held OutputRoot performs the actual read. This resource capability is independent of ambient output authority. Evidence: src/bin/jubarte.rs:2811-2848,2851-2870,2936-2943.

Document-selected font families to renderer/host: renderer searches installed font locations and its configured per-user directory; a persistent index can directly select stored face paths after file/directory stamp checks. JUBARTE_FONT_DIR overrides the platform directory. JUBARTE_FONT_INDEX overrides the index path; empty/off disables it. Otherwise the index is a sibling of fonts, at parent(user_font_dir)/font-index.tsv, with staging at the same path after replacing its extension with tsv.<pid>.tmp. These operations use ambient std::fs and do not pass through MCP OutputRoot. Evidence: src/convert/font.rs:2633-2652,2814-2862,3098-3107,3155-3168,3182-3229.

Browser WASM host to byte API: browser/Node wasm-bindgen functions accept and return byte arrays/strings; filesystem publication is separately performed by a host adapter. The Node CLI explicitly has node:fs authority and directly reads/writes caller-selected paths. Do not transfer native Rust publication guarantees to that adapter. Evidence: jubarte-wasm/src/lib.rs:7-28; jubarte-wasm/cli/bin/jubarte-redlines.mjs:16-21,52-73,76-79,106-110.

Release infrastructure to explicit updater: the target is fixed to jandira-tech/jubarte-redlines and the platform-specific archive entry jubarte-<version>-<target>/jubarte[.exe]. Checksums come from SHA256SUMS.txt in the same release. Current RELEASE_KEYS is empty and FIRST_SIGNED_RELEASE is None, so signatures are not enforced. Noninteractive replacement requires --yes; --check performs lookup only; named versions can intentionally downgrade. An extracted-binary hook rejects nonregular files. Evidence: src/update.rs:25-48,91-108,120-125,144-160,198-257,274-285,299-320.

Maintainer/tag authority to release publication: v* tag pushes run a version-match check, read-only build jobs and a distinct contents:write release job. Signing receives secrets.ZIPSIGN_PRIVATE_KEY in its signing step, decodes keys into a temporary runner directory, removes that directory on exit and verifies against committed public keys when present. GitHub publication receives secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN and uploads dist/* to github.repository. Evidence: .github/workflows/release.yml:15-21,31-49,51-89,230-245,261-309,317-322,356-369.
attackerCapabilities: A document supplier can control document/archive/XML/media/font payloads, Markdown image references and document-selected font families, without controlling the host environment, chosen resource root, installed font index, operator account or release infrastructure. Failure at parsing/layout could add denial of service or unauthorized resource access; those impacts require separate validation.

An MCP caller can read supported documents under the granted root and request exposed editing/rendering writes there, including overwrite=true. This is intentionally granted authority; there is no established tenant or per-tool identity separation. Reading outside the capability or causing writes outside the document root would require a separate control failure or an independently reachable host subsystem.

An attacker who can only supply input documents is not assumed able to set JUBARTE_FONT_DIR/JUBARTE_FONT_INDEX, modify installed font/index files, publish release assets or push tags. Control of those resources is a distinct prerequisite.

A release-asset attacker could affect the updater only when the user invokes update and consumes the affected release. Current checksums provide corruption detection without independent signer authentication, as the documentation explicitly recognizes.
securityObjectives: Refuse malformed or policy-exceeding packages before representative comparison/rendering work; preserve effective overridden limits instead of silently weakening them. Resource limits remain caller/host responsibilities beyond admission. Evidence: src/admission.rs:63-99,439-553; SECURITY.md:39-77.

Keep MCP document reads and outputs within the originally granted directory capability, resist escaping symlink resolution, and require explicit replacement authorization. Distinguish this from renderer ambient font/cache access. Evidence: jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:67-108; src/publication.rs:146-199,431-463; src/convert/font.rs:3182-3229.

Bind prepared edits to their intended source when the relevant guard is supplied or workflow requires it; resolve plan failures before publishing. Publish verified bytes with accurate partial-commit and durability reporting. Evidence: src/edit.rs:5-13,2081-2089; src/bin/jubarte.rs:1642-1655; src/publication.rs:83-130,168-173.
Restrict Markdown image reads to the selected resource root and refuse network image schemes. Evidence: src/bin/jubarte.rs:2811-2870,2936-2943.

Keep updater replacement explicit and platform/version bound, verify checksums and regular-file identity, and enforce signatures if trusted keys are enabled. Limit release publication authority to its privileged job and keep private signing material out of published artifacts. Evidence: src/update.rs:120-125,198-257,274-285,307-320; .github/workflows/release.yml:234-235,261-309,356-369.
assumptions: No exact deployment context or authoritative knowledge base was supplied. The model describes supported code paths, not observed production exposure, remote service access, tenant isolation or active release settings.

Repository SECURITY.md is inherited policy and analysis data. It declares untrusted document inputs and process memory/CPU isolation obligations; this pass does not certify that every exported operation or decoder enforces every declared limit. Evidence: SECURITY.md:39-77.

Documentation/configuration disagreement: MCP build_server says tools only touch files under root, and its module documentation describes outputs under root, but native rendering has ambient font reads and persistent font-index writes outside that root. Preserve both facts: OutputRoot confines document I/O; the process is not globally filesystem confined. Native macOS fonts default to $HOME/Library/Application Support/jubarte/fonts and index to $HOME/Library/Application Support/jubarte/font-index.tsv. Linux uses $XDG_DATA_HOME/jubarte/fonts or $HOME/.local/share/jubarte/fonts with the index in the parent; Windows uses $APPDATA/jubarte/fonts with index in its parent and system fonts from WINDIR/SystemRoot/LOCALAPPDATA. Nonempty JUBARTE_FONT_DIR overrides fonts; JUBARTE_FONT_INDEX explicitly selects index, empty/off disables it. Temporary sibling replaces extension with tsv.<pid>.tmp. Evidence: jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:5-9,67-72,234-236; src/convert/font.rs:2633-2652,2831-2862,3098-3107,3155-3168,3182-3229. No exploit or unauthorized new capability is established by this architectural discrepancy alone.

Documentation/configuration disagreement: crate overview says every function returns bytes with no temp files, whereas native rendering maintains a font index using a temporary sibling file and rename. This does not imply document bytes are written to that index; it records lookup/path/stamp metadata. Evidence: src/lib.rs:7-11; src/convert/font.rs:3090-3096,3192-3229.

Self-update documentation describes signed releases conditionally and explicitly says an empty trusted-key list means checksum-only. Current code matches the staged, checksum-only state; presence of signature dependencies does not establish active signature enforcement. Evidence: docs/SELF_UPDATE.md:29-35,59-80; src/update.rs:44-48,245-249,274-285.

docs/SELF_UPDATE.md:22-24 claims GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN raise the API budget. src/update.rs:198-210 does not explicitly pass an auth token. Whether the dependency automatically consumes these variables was not inspected; credential recipients and this documentation claim remain unresolved.

Actual OS permissions, environment values, MCP launch cwd/root, font availability, writable-cache state, tag protections, GitHub environment approvals and configured secret presence are not established by source alone.

External relationship fetching, all legacy-DOC/media decoders, platform-specific dependency extraction internals, all CLI wrapper publication paths and package-manager publication scripts were not exhaustively inspected. They remain explicit coverage gaps; this is an architecture pass without runtime execution.

scope.summary: Representative product architecture and conditional release/update boundaries in the current repository; architecture mapping is not completed security-audit coverage.

findings.title: Rendering an embedded HTML table can exhaust process memory
findings.summary: Rendering a small DOCX containing an HTML altChunk with a large `colspan` allocates one generated grid column per attacker-supplied span value. A single cell with `colspan="1000000000"` causes a billion string writes before layout, bypassing the original package's input-size budgets.

severity.rationale: A document author can deterministically exhaust CPU and memory in a consuming renderer with a tiny input. Availability impact is high for that process, but remote/shared-service deployment is not established and process limits can contain it.

confidence.rationale: Direct source trace establishes attacker-controlled integer parsing and the unbounded allocation loop after admission; no runtime exploit was executed.

taxonomy.category: Uncontrolled resource consumption during HTML expansion

codeEvidence.label: Admission precedes HTML expansion
codeEvidence.explanation: The renderer loads a relationship-targeted chunk from the admitted package and expands it before DOM layout; generated output has no size gate here.

codeEvidence.label: Chunk bytes become HTML and generated WML
codeEvidence.explanation: Attacker-authored HTML is converted locally into a new WML string; archive inflation bounds do not constrain this representation expansion.

codeEvidence.label: HTML colspan accepted without upper bound
codeEvidence.explanation: Any positive span fitting usize survives unchanged; the lower clamp adds no upper bound.

codeEvidence.label: Span values determine generated grid length
codeEvidence.code:
let cols = table
            .rows
            .iter()
            .map(|r| r.iter().map(|c| c.span).sum::<usize>())
            .max()
            .unwrap_or(1)
            .max(1);
        let col_w = 9360 / cols;
codeEvidence.explanation: A one-cell row sets cols directly to the supplied span, independently of input length.

codeEvidence.label: One string write for each column
codeEvidence.explanation: The attacker-sized loop grows the output string by tens of gigabytes for a billion-column cell before later validation could occur.

rootCause.summary: `with_layout()` admits the original DOCX, then `expand()` loads its HTML chunk and passes it to `html_to_wml()`. Cell parsing stores `colspan` as an unrestricted usize. `end_table()` sums the spans into `cols` and emits a grid element for every column, so a short decimal attribute controls huge CPU and allocation work after the input gate.

findings.remediation: Reject spans and total table column counts above a documented limit before construction; use checked addition and enforce a generated-output/work budget shared across all HTML chunks.

counterEvidence: Admission caps compressed/inflated bytes and XML policy before conversion (src/convert/mod.rs:773-778).
SECURITY.md recommends process memory/CPU isolation, which can limit collateral damage.
No shared or remote renderer deployment is established.
limitations: No application code or resource-exhaustion input was executed.
validation.summary: Parent verified the baseline candidate against the actual converter entrypoint and HTML builder. A well-formed one-cell table with a large positive colspan reaches the grid-generation loop with no upper bound; admission limits only the stored input, not this new output.

controls: Original package admission limits do not bound generated table columns.
Host process resource limits mitigate collateral impact.

dataflow.summary: DOCX main-story altChunk relationship -> embedded HTML bytes -> html_to_wml cell span -> row span sum -> repeated grid-column string writes.

impact.rationale: Renderer process CPU and memory exhaustion; a shared host could lose service if its integration provides no isolation.

likelihood.rationale: The numeric span flows directly to the allocation loop and a small input can request billions of iterations.

reachability.summary: A caller-controlled document is sufficient at public conversion APIs; no privileged options or network access are required. The victim must render/layout the supplied document.
preconditions: Victim invokes a rendering/layout API on attacker-authored DOCX.

attackPath.summary: Provide a DOCX whose main story references an embedded HTML table with a huge numeric colspan, then have a victim render it as PDF/PNG or request layout facts.

remediationTests: Assert that a tiny HTML chunk with a huge colspan is refused before grid allocation.
Cover aggregate span overflow, multiple cells/chunks, and valid spans at the inclusive boundary.

findings.title: Rendering embedded CSS multiplies property allocations per selector
findings.summary: A small HTML altChunk stylesheet can exhaust renderer memory before layout. `parse_css()` deep-copies every property value into a separate map for every selector, including unused selectors and unsupported property names; thousands of selectors can retain thousands of copies of one large value.

severity.rationale: Attacker-authored document content can reliably exhaust the consuming process with a modest input. Shared-service deployment is conditional and host process limits reduce collateral impact.

confidence.rationale: Source shows owned String property values, HashMap::clone per selector and retention in Builder with no count or allocation budget.

taxonomy.category: Uncontrolled resource amplification in stylesheet parsing

codeEvidence.label: CSS properties stored as owned strings
codeEvidence.code:
let props: Props = body
            .split(';')
            .filter_map(|d| d.split_once(':'))
            .map(|(k, v)| (k.trim().to_ascii_lowercase(), v.trim().to_string()))
            .collect();
codeEvidence.explanation: A large attacker property value becomes a retained owned String without filtering supported properties or limiting value size.

codeEvidence.label: Deep clone for every selector
codeEvidence.explanation: Distinct comma-separated selectors each retain a deep clone of the complete property map. Allocation is selector count times property bytes.

codeEvidence.label: All styles parsed before body import
codeEvidence.explanation: The parser retains every rule before examining body content, so selectors need not match any element to trigger the allocation.

codeEvidence.label: Admission precedes HTML expansion
codeEvidence.explanation: The renderer loads a relationship-targeted chunk from the admitted package and expands it before DOM layout; generated output has no size gate here.

codeEvidence.label: Chunk bytes become HTML and generated WML
codeEvidence.explanation: Attacker-authored HTML is converted locally into a new WML string; archive inflation bounds do not constrain this representation expansion.

rootCause.summary: After DOCX admission, `expand()` imports an embedded HTML chunk. `html_to_wml()` eagerly calls `parse_css()`, which owns property values as Strings and calls `props.clone()` for every selector. Each distinct selector retains a full copy, making retained memory proportional to selector count multiplied by property size rather than bounded by the original part.

findings.remediation: Share immutable declaration blocks between selectors and enforce aggregate stylesheet work/allocation budgets, selector-count and value-length limits before allocating. Ignore unsupported properties before retention.

counterEvidence: Package input/inflation limits constrain the original HTML but not selector-value multiplication.
Process limits recommended by SECURITY.md can contain the failure.
validation.summary: Parent verified that selector keys are distinct, values are owned Strings, clones remain in Builder, and no maximum or supported-property filter limits the copies. A stylesheet with 10,000 short selectors and one 1 MiB property requests about 10 GiB of retained property bytes from about 1.1 MiB HTML.

dataflow.summary: DOCX chunk -> html_to_wml -> parse_css -> owned property map -> full cloned map retained under each selector.

reachability.summary: Public PDF/PNG/layout conversion loads relationship-targeted HTML after admission. Attacker needs only to supply the document; unused selectors still trigger parsing.

attackPath.summary: Embed a stylesheet containing many distinct comma-separated selectors and a long property value in a DOCX altChunk, then have a victim render the document.

remediationTests: Assert that many selectors sharing a large declaration block remain bounded or are refused before multiplication.
Cover unused selectors, unsupported property names, multiple style blocks, and valid boundary inputs.

originalCandidates.title: Embedded HTML CSS causes multiplicative retained property allocation
originalCandidates.message: parse_css lines 158-166 builds one Props map then deep-clones every property/value for each comma selector. E.g. <style>.s0,...,.s9999{a:<1 MiB value>}</style> is ~1.1 MiB admitted HTML but retains ~10 GiB value clones before any body rendering. html_to_wml lines 607-610 eagerly parses all styles, even unused selectors/properties. Separate CPU/memory multiplier from colspan.

findings.title: Scanning a document for leaks can abort on deeply nested XML
findings.summary: Calling public `scrub::leaks()` on an attacker-supplied package can overflow the process stack. It bounds archive bytes but sends XML directly to the recursive permissive DOM parser without checking the XML depth policy.

severity.rationale: A small malicious XML part can reliably abort the consumer process. Exposure is the public Rust leak-scan API; no remote/shared-service deployment is assumed.

confidence.rationale: The direct public API trace has only ZIP byte/count gates before an unbounded recursive parser call. Runtime stack threshold was not measured.

taxonomy.category: Missing XML depth validation before recursive parsing

codeEvidence.label: Public leak scan opens bytes directly
codeEvidence.code:

rootCause.summary: `decode_image()` routes embedded WMF bytes to `raster_wmf()`. codeEvidence.explanation: After indexing, only a count smaller than declared is refused; excess indexed entries and concealed duplicate collapse survive.

codeEvidence.label: Only declared count gates indexing
codeEvidence.explanation: Only the parsed total count is compared to max_entries before archive indexing.

rootCause.summary: `declared_entry_count()` reads ZIP32 EOCD total entries at +10, and `preindex_budget()` compares only that value to max_entries. The pinned reader instead uses entries-on-this-disk at +8. Admission then tests only indexed count < declared, without comparing counts for equality or enforcing the effective indexed count. The reader's name map also collapses exact raw-name duplicates, so manipulated totals conceal that shortfall.

findings.remediation: Require consistent single-disk ZIP32/ZIP64 counts before indexing using the reader's effective-footer rules. Enforce actual indexed count afterward, and detect raw duplicates directly or through the dependency's duplicate indicator.

counterEvidence: This ZIP32 construction is limited to 65,535 indexed records.
Compressed input and actual inflation limits remain effective.
Distinct surviving case/decoded-name collisions are still rejected.
The custom archive consistency pass does not invoke zip's separate duplicate-flag validator.
limitations: No application code or crafted archive was executed.
validation.method: independent static source trace including offline pinned dependency
validation.summary: With 20,000 real entries, +8=20,000 and +10=1, the 10,000-entry preindex gate sees 1 while zip indexes all 20,000. Its count is not <1. Exact duplicate collapse is similarly concealed. Parent inspected zip-9.0.5/src/read/mod.rs:69-71 (disk count), format/blocks.rs:332-360 and format/find_central_directory.rs:175-209 (no equality check), and read/zip_archive.rs:271-299 (indexing count). Its IndexMap insertion replaces exact raw names at read/zip_archive.rs:81-86.

dataflow.summary: Caller ZIP -> total-count preindex gate -> disk-count dependency indexing -> one-sided shortfall test -> excess entries or collapsed duplicates accepted.

reachability.summary: Public DOCX admission and PartFs loading share this gate, without privileged limit overrides.

attackPath.summary: Supply a ZIP32 DOCX preserving its true +8 count but reducing the +10 total used by admission.

remediationTests: Reject disagreeing +8/+10 counts with excess unique entries and exact duplicate names.
Cover ZIP64 footer selection and inclusive valid entry limits.

originalCandidates.message: admission::declared_entry_count reads ZIP32 EOCD count at +10; pinned zip9.0.5 read/mod.rs:69-71 indexes number_of_files_on_this_disk at +8. No equality check. >10,000 unique empty entries with +8 true count and +10=1 pass preindex, ZipArchive indexes all, admit only tests archive.len()<declared not >max_entries. PartFs also relies on preindex. Byte budgets remain.
